Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-09): "btw the new codex provider should have auto review and context_management". The Codex provider HolyAgent ships has Codex auto-review (tool calls reviewed by the codex-auto-review reviewer) and context_management (Codex server-side compaction) while keeping apply_patch plus the just-bash bash and Pi read, edit and write; pi-codex-conversion applyPatchOnly mode turns native compaction off, so the plan must provide both another way.

Conflict found (assignment-0mw96qjlf-o4zi): Billion Context cancels Pi compaction and rewrites outgoing requests, openai-codex-responses included, so it clashes with Codex context_management (server-side compaction with an encrypted item replayed); its bash guardrails (60 s default timeout, 50 KB output cap) also apply to the just-bash bash tool by name.

Decided (maintainer, verbatim, 2026-11-09): "btw billion context probably conflicts with context management, if they don't work similarly prefer billion, if they do prefer context management". They work differently: Billion Context compresses the history client-side through its proxy and keeps it retrievable (compress, decompress, search_context tools), while Codex context_management replaces the history with an opaque encrypted server-side compaction item that cannot be searched or expanded. So Billion Context is preferred: while it is on (pi.features.contextCompression, the default) the Codex provider sends no context_management, and context_management is used only when Billion Context is off.

result:
result: 2 blockers. The route table matches the approved one, and `mise run verify` passes, but Codex specialists lose their web tools and `apply_patch` can delete a file.

**Built-in /code-review:** I ran it on `bb412cc...9d54902` and it loaded as the built-in. It returned 10 findings, classified below.

**Blocking**
1. `packages/integrations/pi/src/agents.ts:54`. The `gpt-6` agent files are generated from the default Kimi config. `dist/families/gpt-6/agents/librarian-research.md:6` and `librarian-lookup.md` list `ext:pi-provider-kimi-code/moonshot_search` and `moonshot_fetch`. Codex loads no Kimi extension, and `webChoice` picks `pi-web-kit`, so no agent file lists `web_search` or `web_fetch`.
   - The package treats an `ext:` entry as an explicit allowlist, so Librarian and the other Search specialists end up with no web tools under Codex. I read the code and did not run it.
   - No test covers this, and the `codex-provider.test.ts` web test only checks `webChoice`.
   - Fix: build the family agent files from a Codex config, or map web entries per provider. Add a test that a Codex Librarian lists `ext:pi-web-kit/web_search`.
2. `packages/runtime/src/pi/codex/apply-patch.ts:400`. An Update File whose `Move to` equals its own path stages the new text and then stages `null` for the same key. The file is deleted and the summary reports `M`. I confirmed this by reading. No test covers it. Fix: treat a same-path move as a plain update, with a test.

**Non-blocking**
`apply-patch.ts:408`. The write phase is not atomic, so a mid-write failure leaves a partial patch. The tool description at line 26 promises "whole or not at all", which overclaims. Reword it or add a rollback.
`apply-patch.ts:381`. The path guard is lexical, so a symlink inside the project can still point outside it. Pi's own `write` and `edit` have no guard at all, so this is acceptable.
`codex.ts:197` and `luna-reserve.ts:31`. `reserve` is not cleared on `session_start`. The usage-limit regex also matches a transient `rate_limit_exceeded`, though the banner check still gates the switch.
`codex.ts` (`toReserve`). Every request is rewritten to `gpt-reserve`, including Sol and Terra requests at `xhigh`, and the effort is not clamped.
`context-management.ts:117`. The checkpoint check compares only the count and the last covered item, a heuristic that could replay a stale compaction item.
`extension.ts:1269`. `apply_patch` is activated once and any failure is ignored silently.
`codex.ts:82`. This code uses `node:fs/promises` and async closures. Lint passes and it sits at the Pi boundary, so it is a Bun-preference nit.
`schema.ts:252`. The `pi` section encodes as the identity, so resolved route rows would be written back as explicit values on a re-encode. I could not confirm that any config-write path does this, so it is a note only.
Auto-review is not in this commit; the writer defers it to a later PR. Context management has no switch of its own, only Billion Context off. Both bear on the "own module, can be turned off on its own" requirement.

**Judged points**
**Route table:** all 19 rows match the approved table, and the tests assert each row.
**context_management gating:** it is sent only for Codex while Billion Context is off. The compaction item is replayed and dropped on `session_start`, `session_compact` and `session_tree`.
**Luna Reserve:** a wrong usage endpoint or banner fails safe, because the reserve never opens. A wrong `gpt-reserve` model id would leave the session on a failing model, because a failed status check keeps the reserve. This is acceptable only because both values are flagged as unverified.
**Kimi:** it is unchanged. `KIMI_ROUTES` is untouched, the default provider is Kimi, and all existing suites pass.
**Setup screen:** the Luna Reserve row shows under Kimi too. The description says "Codex provider only", so I accept it.

evidence:
The Codex provider meets the requirements and the approved route table: `packages/runtime/src/pi/codex/routes.ts` matches the approved table and `codex-provider.test.ts` asserts it, but blockers 1 and 2 above fail the behavior bar.
Kimi and existing defaults behave unchanged: `KIMI_ROUTES` untouched, default provider still `kimi-coding-global`, existing Kimi suites pass.
Tests cover the change and fail without it: the new test files cover routes, apply_patch, gating and reserve, but nothing covers the Codex agent-file web tools or a same-path move, so the tests are incomplete for blockers 1 and 2.
